title: Design System: Darin — Civic Evidence Desk

display.purpose: The DARIN wordmark (masthead) and modal titles. Fraunces speaks.

title.purpose: Card headlines — the one line read mid-call. ≤60 characters. Fraunces.

say.purpose: The say-this line only — a quotation, so Fraunces italic.

body.purpose: Bullets, hints, rows, buttons, general UI. Libre Franklin.

longform.purpose: Post-meeting outputs only — editorial sizing, ≤70ch. Libre Franklin.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked mono section titles, the SAY label, docket entries.

micro.purpose: Speaker tags and card-type chips. Plex Mono, stamped.

mono.purpose: Live transcript, streaming output, paths, templates. The record.

shadows.name: toast-float
shadows.purpose: The single floating surface. Panels are flat; depth is drawn with rules.

shadows.name: attention-seal
shadows.purpose: Urgent NOW card arrival; pulses exactly twice, then stops.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input focus, with border shifting to federal blue.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Default utilitarian transition on all interactive elements.

motion.name: card-expire
motion.purpose: Proactive card expiry fade before removal.

motion.name: attention-seal
motion.purpose: Urgent NOW arrival. Pulses twice, never again.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: REC stamp and watcher-thinking dot. Live state only (Ink-Means-Alive).

narrative.overview: Darin is a public-records inspection desk for a live conversation: every card is a stamped record slid across warm paper, case-labeled, dated, sourced, legible in a glance. One identity, two materials — Desk (record paper, navy ink) and After Hours (lamplit navy, paper text), toggled from the masthead; typography, shapes, and the signal vocabulary never change, only material tokens. Color is stamp ink with one meaning per hue; brass is furniture. There is no glow anywhere — liveness is a fresh stamp.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper (or lamplit navy) surfaces structured by hairline rules — flat, printed, physical
Stamp-ink color as a strict signal vocabulary (six inks, one meaning each; brass is furniture)
Motion reserved for live state; paper never animates while nothing is happening
Three-voice typography: Fraunces speaks, Libre Franklin explains, IBM Plex Mono files
Glance-first hierarchy: headline → say-this line → everything else subordinate

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each stamp ink has exactly one semantic meaning and is prohibited elsewhere. Brass is exempt because brass means nothing — and must never be pressed into meaning something.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Inks touch paper as 10–26% color-mix tints with matching tinted 1px borders, or as small solid marks. Full-saturation fills are reserved for the three command buttons. No gradients, ever.

rules.name: The Ink-Step Rule
rules.body: Any accent used as text must use its designated -text token, verified ≥4.5:1 on its actual surface in both materials. Base hues are for marks; ink steps are for words.

rules.name: The Two-Materials Rule
rules.body: Components reference only semantic tokens; the theme switch swaps token values and nothing else. A component that hard-codes a material color or changes shape/typography/meaning between materials is a bug.

rules.name: The Three-Second Rule
rules.body: Any text met mid-call must land in under three seconds of split attention: headlines ≤60 characters, ≤3 bullets, no paragraphs in cards. Editorial sizing belongs to post-meeting output only.

rules.name: The Voice Rule
rules.body: Fraunces only for what could be said aloud; Plex Mono only for what belongs in the record; Libre Franklin for everything between.

rules.name: The Ink-Means-Alive Rule
rules.body: Motion and fresh marks are reserved for things live, armed, or urgent right now. Static paper never pulses, never animates, never shines.

dos: Do keep every stamp ink on its one meaning: federal blue = interactive/ME, ledger teal = THEM/proactive, ochre = urgent, approval green = go/live, inspection red = record/stop, notary violet = post-meeting.
Do route every component color through semantic tokens so both materials stay correct; verify new pairs in both materials.
Do use the -text ink steps whenever an accent becomes text.
Do keep the case pocket's glance order: stamp → headline → say-this → bullets → cues → docket line.
Do hold WCAG AA in both materials, with focus rings, hover states, and reduced-motion alternatives.
donts: Don't build anything that reads as chatbot UI — no bubbles, no avatar personality, no conversational framing.
Don't build anything that reads as a SaaS dashboard — no KPI grids, no hero metrics, no analytics chrome.
Don't use gradients, glassmorphism, neon, or glow — ink doesn't glow; depth is drawn, never cast (toast excepted).
Don't make anything pill-shaped, decorate with emoji, or let the materials drift apart in shape, type, or meaning.
Don't cross the voices or exceed the Three-Second Rule on live surfaces.
